The test image shows soybean leaves with prominent interveinal necrosis — brown/tan dead tissue between green veins, affecting multiple leaves, with necrosis spreading from margins inward. The veins remain somewhat green while the tissue between them is dead/brown. This pattern strongly suggests Sudden Death Syndrome or Brown Stem Rot.

Let me view reference images starting with the top candidates.
Good match — SDS shows interveinal necrosis with green veins and brown tissue between. Let me check Brown Stem Rot and a couple other candidates.
This SDS reference (268) is very close to the test image — same interveinal necrosis pattern with green veins and brown tissue. Let me check a few more classes to be thorough.

Now I have enough evidence to make my decision.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: Soybean leaves with classic interveinal necrosis — brown/tan dead tissue between green veins, affecting multiple leaflets simultaneously, with leaf curl and severe tissue death
- SDS reference (268): Near-perfect match — same green veins with brown interveinal necrosis pattern, same multi-leaflet presentation
- Brown Stem Rot reference (18): Also shows interveinal necrosis but more yellow/chlorotic; also BSR_103 shows stem internal browning (not leaf focus)
- All other classes clearly don't match: Cercospora = small spots, Septoria = yellowed leaves with dark spots, Frogeye = circular eye-shaped spots, Bacterial Pustule = small pustules, Phyllosticta = large marginal lesions with circular spots, Vein Necrosis = small isolated spots, Phytophthora = whole plant wilt

The interveinal necrosis with green veins intact, affecting multiple leaflets across the canopy, is the hallmark of Sudden Death Syndrome. SDS_268 is visually nearly identical to the test image.
